questions.text: If Direct Mail generated 27,200 leads in 2003, how many were generated by Radio Advertising that year?
questions.explanation: Direct Mail was 8.5% of 2003 leads, so total = 27,200 ÷ 0.085 = 320,000. Radio Advertising was 20% in 2003 → 20% × 320,000 = 64,000.

flag.note: The chart shows Radio Advertising at 20% in 2003 (10% is 2004). 20% × 320,000 = 64,000 (D). PDF key B uses the 2004 figure. PDF working: Radio Advertising = 10% of 320,000 = 32,000.

questions.text: If eMarketing generated 100,000 leads in 2004 (an increase of 25% from 2003), how many leads were generated by Newspaper Advertising in 2003?
If the number of leads generated by Direct Mail in 2004 was half that generated by eMarketing in 2003, when eMarketing accounted for 80,000 leads, how many did Telemarketing generate in 2004?
questions.explanation: Direct Mail 2004 = 80,000 ÷ 2 = 40,000, which is 10% of 2004 leads. Telemarketing was 40%, i.e. 4× Direct Mail → 160,000.

questions.text: If in 2004 the number of leads generated was 15% higher overall, and Radio Advertising generated 46,000, how many would Newspaper Advertising have generated?
questions.explanation: The '15% higher overall' is a distractor: shares stay the same. In 2004 Radio = 10% and Newspaper = 15%, so Newspaper = 46,000 × 15/10 = 69,000.

questions.text: Approximately what share of the total revenue for the five years displayed was generated in 2004?
Approximately what share of the 2002 web-based revenue was generated by 3rd Party Bookings?

By how much would the total 3rd Party Bookings in 2004 have to be increased to generate the same revenue from web-based bookings as was made via the Direct Bookings route? (Assume the Total to Web-based bookings ratio remains the same for both routes.)
questions.explanation: 3rd Party 2004: web 30 of total 300 (1 : 10). To match Direct web-based revenue of 52.5, the 3rd Party total would need to be 525 — an increase of 225. 225 isn't an option, so the answer is 'None of these'.

flag.note: The question asks for the increase, which is 525 − 300 = 225 (not an option → E 'None of these'). Key C (525) is the new total, not the increase.

questions.text: For which manufacturing plant(s) are the Administration : Rent costs in the ratio 12:5?
For the Glasgow manufacturing plant, which maintenance cost(s) represent approximately 7% of the total costs?
What is the average annual cost for servicing each of the 5 manufacturing plants (assume 4 weeks in a month)?
questions.explanation: Average weekly servicing = (1,050 + 1,100 + 950 + 1,025 + 875) ÷ 5 = 1,000. 4 weeks × 12 months = 48 weeks → £48,000.

questions.text: Which two manufacturing plants have the same total maintenance costs per week?
questions.explanation: Weekly totals: Midlands 2,816; Bordeaux 2,790; Berlin 2,451; Amsterdam 2,799; Glasgow 2,704. No two are equal.
